page: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is a graphics-intensive instance type built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 2.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance integrates four NVIDIA Blackwell RTX Pro 6000 GPUs with a combined 384 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of 7600 GB of NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 400 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for matrix math acceleration. In CPU benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 21470.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 91429.15. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 reaches a top-tier rate of 564.58 GB/sec, while single-core performance sits in the average tier with a stress-ng single-core score of 2106.88.

Memory performance is characterized by a strong PassMark memory score of 2809.93 and a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 6648.45 GB/sec. The four NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs deliver top-tier results in specialized tasks, including a Geekbench ray tracing score of 95118.0 and an image processing score of 21579.0. Large-scale language model inference benchmarks show top-tier throughput, processing 1278.65 tokens per second for prompts and generating 28.21 tokens per second using a 70B parameter model.

Given the high density of premium hardware components, including DDR5 memory, massive NVMe SSD storage, and four Blackwell GPUs, this instance represents a high-resource tier where cost is balanced against parallel processing capabilities. The primary tradeoff is the average single-core CPU performance relative to its top-tier multi-core and GPU capabilities. This profile is suited for large-scale LLM inference, real-time ray tracing, graphics-intensive rendering, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
